items.entity: Configuration-1 load on the free face (the face opposite the fixed face)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the loads are 'applied to the side opposite to a fixed one (Fig.1(A, D))'. Where configuration 1's load sits on that face is shown only in the 'Initial BVP' panel (Fig. 2(A)), which is not available. The text calls one configuration 'symmetric' and the other 'non-symmetric' but never says which one is configuration 1. The Fig. 3 caption puts an xz symmetry plane in both examples, which suggests the load is centred across the width (y = 0.5).
readings: Centre of the free face, (y/L, z/L) = (0.5, 0.5): the 'symmetric' case
Midpoint of the lower (or upper) edge of the free face, (y/L, z/L) = (0.5, 0) or (0.5, 1): symmetric only about the xz mid-plane, the 'non-symmetric' case
Along the whole lower edge of the free face (z/L = 0, y/L from 0 to 1)
Spread over the entire free face

items.description: Sec. 4.1 never says whether the load is a concentrated force, a small traction patch, a line load or a uniform face traction. Sec. 4.2 explicitly uses concentrated forces, but Sec. 4.1 does not, and it blames the slow GMRES convergence on the mixed boundary conditions. Boundary tractions are piecewise constant over voxel-face triangles, so even a 'point' load would cover at least one voxel face, and the patch size is not given.
readings: Concentrated force at a single grid node
Uniform traction on one voxel face (1/64 x 1/64 of the side)
Uniform traction on a small patch, e.g. 2x2 to 4x4 voxel faces (1/32 to 1/16 of the side)
Line load along one edge of the free face
Uniform traction over the whole free face

items.description: The load direction is never stated; it is shown only in Fig. 2(A). Two hints, neither explicit: the Fig. 3 caption ('xz cross section passing through symmetry plane') suggests the load lies in the xz plane, and the claimed agreement with classic cantilever solutions [23, 24, 4] suggests a bending load.
readings: Transverse to the cantilever axis, in the xz symmetry plane (e.g. -z): bending
Transverse along y (normal to the xz plane)
Normal to the loaded face (axial tension or compression), as in the uniform-tension Fig. 1(A) model the text literally cites
Oblique in the xz plane (transverse plus axial components)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives no force or traction value. Results are reported only as the normalised Psi/Psi0 (Fig. 2(F)).
readings: Total force F = 1
Unit traction |t| = 1 on the loaded area (total force equals the loaded area)

items.description: Sec. 2.3 and Algorithm 1 turn every voxel with D^T < D_min + C(D_max - D_min) to void. C is 'chosen empirically' ('Typically, C=0.001÷0.1') and controls the removal rate per iteration and the level of detail; Sec. 5 says results 'strongly depend' on it. Sec. 4.1 gives no value of C and only says the design was reached after three iterations.
readings: C tuned so that alpha first drops below 0.6 at the third iteration

items.entity: Final material volume fraction of the reported configuration-1 design
items.description: alpha_c = 0.6 is stated (Sec. 4.1, Fig. 2 caption). But Algorithm 1 breaks at the first iterate with alpha < alpha_c (after the voxel clean-up), and the result came from only three large hard-kill steps. So the actual volume fraction of the design in Fig. 2(B) is somewhat below 0.6 and is not reported.
readings: Volume constraint exactly 0.6
Slightly below 0.6 (the first hard-kill iterate below alpha_c, e.g. 0.5 to 0.6)

items.entity: Figure references for the cantilever BVP and results in Sec. 4.1
items.description: Sec. 4.1 cites Fig. 1(A, D) for the initial BVPs, Fig. 1(B,E), 1(C) and 1(F) for the results, and Fig. 2(A, B) for the TD fields. The captions put the uniform-tension benchmark cube and performance plots in Fig. 1, the cantilevers in Fig. 2 and the TD fields in Fig. 3. Taken literally, configuration 1's BVP would be the Fig. 1(A) uniform-tension cube.
readings: Numbering is off by one: configuration-1 BVP is Fig. 2(A), solution Fig. 2(B), TD field Fig. 3(A)
Literal reading: configuration-1 BVP is Fig. 1(A), i.e. uniform normal tension on the face opposite the fixed face

items.entity: Voxels under the load and next to the fixed face
items.description: Algorithm 1 removes any voxel below the TD threshold and never mentions non-design regions. The text does not say whether the loaded voxels or a layer at the fixed face must stay solid.
readings: No passive regions: all 64^3 voxels can be removed
Loaded voxel(s) or load patch kept solid (non-design)
A one-voxel solid layer kept at the fixed face and/or around the load

items.entity: Per-iteration post-processing ('excluding isolated voxels and surface irregularities')
items.description: Sec. 2.3 applies this post-processing before alpha and Psi are computed. It does not define the connectivity rule, what counts as a surface irregularity, or whether voxels are only removed or also added back.
readings: Remove solid voxels with no face-connected solid neighbour
Also remove one-voxel spikes and fill one-voxel pits
Remove solid clusters not connected to the fixed face
No clean-up

items.entity: Density/sensitivity filter (regularisation) on the structured grid
items.description: The paper uses no explicit filter: Sec. 5 notes the 'absence of explicit regularization', and C acts as an implicit regulariser. A structured-grid FEM compliance solver normally needs a filter radius to avoid checkerboards, and the text gives no equivalent value.
readings: No filter (pure TD hard-kill thresholding, as in the paper)
Filter radius about 1.5 voxel sizes (about 1.5/64 of the side)
Filter radius about 2 to 3 voxel sizes
